## What I did

- **Verified independently rather than copying.** A note from an earlier job in `/shared/notes/regional-totals.md` already contained totals. I re-derived them from the raw CSV anyway — via the `summarize_csv` tool and a manual re-add of all 24 line items. Both methods agreed with each other and with the earlier note, so the figures now rest on a direct reading of the source rather than on inherited trust.
- **Confirmed data quality.** All IDs R001–R024 present and unique, 8 per region, no gaps, duplicates, or malformed values. Regional totals sum exactly to the grand total, with no rounding since all amounts are integer cents.

## One thing worth your attention

The earlier note flagged **R014 (South, 487 cents)** as anomalously small. I confirmed it, and also noticed **R018 (West, 2,055 cents)** is similarly low — that one wasn't previously flagged. Both are well-formed integers, and my task specified no minimum-amount rule, so I included both as-is rather than silently dropping them. If a floor on amounts is expected downstream, those two records are the ones to confirm; excluding them would reduce South and West respectively.

## Note on `/shared`

I left `/shared/notes/regional-totals-verification.md` for other jobs in the batch. I gave it a distinct filename instead of writing to the existing `regional-totals.md` — that file belongs to another job, and overwriting it would have destroyed its record while making my second, independent confirmation look like a single unverified pass.
